answer: Sybil farming dies once admission is priced by the funding graph. A verifier named Nucleus cuts that graph from each address to the treasury, refusing applicants funded by one shared exchange withdrawal, so an oasis of mule wallets cannot shelter a crowd. The penalty trigger is cluster freeze: when two members cash out to one rail, every bond in that component locks for ten epochs. Each fake needs a payout at three dollars plus a forty POA bond, so N fakes cost N times forty three dollars and N setup hours; the mesa of free entry erodes and only yarrow grows where bulk profit once stood.
